To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the optimal contract is a function of the relative variance of labor productivity and the cost of collecting information about labor productivity.
the optimal wage adjustment scheme is the wage indexation scheme if and only if the cost of information is zero.
wage contracts with incomplete and costly information are optimal if and only if the cost of information is less than a certain threshold.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a model of a wage contract that takes into account both the cost of collecting information and the cost of last minute negotiation.
the interaction of wage indexation with costly information collection and the resulting implications for the optimal contract.
the optimal wage adjustment scheme in a world characterized both by incomplete information and costs of information collection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the wage contract scheme is superior to the wage indexation scheme if and only if the cost of information is sufficiently large relative to the cost of last minute wage negotiation, and if and only if relative variances are sufficiently high relative to aggregate volatility.
wage contracts are optimal when information costs are high and when the labor market is not competitive.
the optimal wage adjustment scheme depends on both the costs of information collection and aggregate volatility.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the optimal wage contract is a function of the cost of information and the cost of wage negotiation.

the optimal wage indexation scheme, in the sense that it is the best contract that is consistent with incomplete information, is a function of relative volatility and costs of information collection, and the optimal adjustment scheme, in the same sense, is a function also of aggregate volatility.
the optimal contract is characterized by the use of information, the cost of its collection, the volatility of the economy, and the cost of last minute wage negotiation.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in an environment with costly information collection, wage indexation is a more efficient adjustment scheme, whereas in a costless information collection environment, wage negotiation is a more efficient scheme.
the optimal wage contract scheme is a hybrid one that combines wage indexation and last minute wage bargaining.
the optimal indexation is not necessarily the one that maximizes expected utility.
